_about: Facet guides (includes/facet-guides.php): the words that make one facet page -- /explore/perth/spa/cold-plunge/ -- its own page. Keyed by the facet's URL slug. 'phrase' is what the search result title leads with ('Ice Baths & Cold Plunges in Perth -- 25 Places'); 'intro' is a list of paragraphs that replaces the category's intro on that page (the 7 intros in specialty-intros.json are used when there is none here); 'faq' is a list of {q, a} shown with FAQPage markup; 'see_also' is a list of {category, facet, label, line} links. House rule: what a session involves, what it costs, where -- never what it does to a body. Every price or fact must come from the listed places or their own sites.

intro: Looking for cold therapy in Perth? {count} places here list an ice bath or cold plunge, and they fall into three kinds of room. Recovery studios, most of this list, sell the plunge by the session, usually alongside a sauna and often other equipment such as compression boots or red light. Bathhouses and a few day spas include an ice bath in a circuit with a sauna, steam room or hot bath. And a handful of gyms, yoga and Pilates studios keep a plunge beside the training floor.

The biggest difference between them is whether you share. Some sessions are communal, with a group in the same sauna and pools at a set time, often for a flat hour; others are booked as a private room for one or two people, and a few places can be hired outright for a group. Each listing says which where the place publishes it.

Where a session price is published, a sauna-and-plunge block starts at about $25 for thirty minutes and an hour runs about $35 to $45, with cheaper early-morning sessions at some rooms and packs or memberships at most. Each place sets its own prices and they change, so check before you go.

Swimwear is required at communal bathhouses, towels and change rooms vary, and some places set a minimum age. Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: How much does an ice bath cost in Perth?
faq.a: Where it's published, a sauna-and-cold-plunge session starts at about $25 for thirty minutes and runs to about $45 for a private hour, with cheaper early-morning sessions at some rooms and packs or memberships at most. Each place sets its own price, and the listing shows it where the place publishes one.

faq.q: Is an ice bath the same as a cold plunge?
faq.a: Perth places use the two names for the same thing: cold water you sit in for a short time. Some use chilled plunge pools, others ice baths or ice showers, and one beach-based operator uses the ocean itself. This page lists them all together.

faq.q: Is an ice bath the same as cryotherapy?
faq.a: No. An ice bath or cold plunge is cold water you sit in. Cryotherapy means standing in a chamber of very cold, dry air for a few minutes, and only a handful of Perth recovery studios offer it. They have their own page: cryotherapy in Perth.

faq.q: Can I book an ice bath privately?
faq.a: Yes, at several places. Some rooms are booked for one person or a pair, and a few can be hired outright for a group; others run communal sessions at set times. The listing says which where the place publishes it.

faq.q: What should I bring?
faq.a: Usually swimwear, which is required at communal bathhouses. Showers, towels and change rooms are common but not universal, so check the place's own website before your first visit.

faq.q: Where can I do an ice bath and sauna together?
faq.a: Most places on this page pair the plunge with a sauna. The ones set up for alternating the two in one session are also listed under Ice bath & sauna together (contrast therapy).

intro: Contrast sessions alternate heat and cold in one booking: a sauna or hot plunge, then an ice bath or cold plunge, repeated in rounds. {count} places in Perth say on their own websites that they run sessions this way.

The format varies more than the name suggests. Some rooms are booked privately for an hour for one or two people; one suburban studio opens from 5am to 9pm, early enough for before work; a dedicated recovery centre pairs a magnesium hot plunge with cold plunge pools; and a beachside operator runs communal hour-long sessions where, at some sites, the cold water is the ocean.

Where prices are published, a private one-hour session is $45 for one and $80 for two at one studio, and thirty minutes in an infrared sauna starts at $25 at another. Packs and memberships bring the per-visit cost down at most places.
Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: What is contrast therapy?
faq.a: Alternating heat and cold in one session, usually a sauna or hot pool and then an ice bath or cold plunge, repeated a few times. How many rounds, and how long each lasts, is set by each place and often left to you.

faq.q: Where can I do an ice bath and sauna in Perth?
faq.a: The {count} places on this page run both for contrast sessions. Many more have one or the other: see Ice baths & cold plunges and Saunas in Perth.

faq.q: How much does a contrast session cost?
faq.a: Where it's published: a private hour is $45 for one and $80 for two at one Perth studio, and thirty minutes of sauna starts at $25 at another. Most places sell packs and memberships that lower the price per visit.

faq.q: Can I book privately or as a group?
faq.a: Both exist. Some places book the room privately for one or two people, several take group bookings or can be hired outright, and others run communal sessions at set times.

intro: A traditional sauna heats the air in a wood-lined room, and in Perth it turns up in four quite different settings: dedicated sauna houses and studios; communal saunas beside the beach; bathhouses, where it's one stop in a circuit with a steam room and baths; and hotel and day spas, where it usually comes with a treatment or a day visit, often in separate men's and women's areas.

Most of the {count} places here pair the heat with cold water, whether an ice bath, a cold plunge or a magnesium pool, and one sauna house runs its sessions around aufguss, where a facilitator works steam and scent through the room in rounds.

Where prices are published, a sauna-and-plunge session starts at about $25 for thirty minutes and an hour is about $35, and one Subiaco room discounts its 5am to 7am sessions. Communal beachside sessions often run a flat hour.

Bring swimwear for communal and bathhouse sessions, check whether towels are supplied, and note that some places set a minimum age: sixteen at one hotel spa, eighteen at one bathhouse. Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: Where is there a Finnish sauna in Perth?
faq.a: Several places on this page describe their sauna as Finnish, including a sauna house built around aufguss sessions, a communal bathhouse and a dedicated recovery centre. Each listing says what kind of sauna it has.

faq.q: Are there saunas at the beach in Perth?
faq.a: Yes. Beachside operators run communal sauna sessions at several Perth beaches, including Scarborough, City Beach, Cottesloe and South Beach, and at some sites the ocean is the cold plunge.

faq.q: How long is a sauna session?
faq.a: Usually booked as a block. Thirty minutes and an hour are the most common lengths published, and communal beachside sessions often run a flat hour.

faq.q: Can day visitors use a hotel spa's sauna?
faq.a: At some. At least one CBD hotel spa is open to day visitors as well as hotel guests; others are by appointment with a treatment. Check the listing and the spa's own website.

intro: {count} places in Perth list an infrared sauna, and most of them book the cabin privately: you have the room to yourself, or share it with one other person, for a timed session. That is the main practical difference from a traditional sauna, which runs at a much higher air temperature and is more often a shared room.

Most are recovery studios, where the sauna sits beside an ice bath, red light or compression boots and can be booked with them. The rest are day spas and float centres that offer it alongside other treatments, plus a few physio and Pilates studios. One Claremont clinic uses a one-person pod with your head outside instead of a cabin.

Where a single-session price is published, thirty minutes costs $25 to $40 at most places, and $25 at studios in Beldon and Cockburn Central. Forty-five minutes is usually $35 to $50. Bringing a second person into the cabin generally adds $10 to $30 rather than doubling the price. Several studios publish only packs or memberships, and sauna-and-ice-bath sessions are priced separately. Prices were checked on the places' own websites in October 2026, and each place sets its own, so check before you book.

Because most cabins are private, light clothing, swimwear or a towel is the norm. Bring water, and check whether towels are supplied. Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: How much does an infrared sauna cost in Perth?
faq.a: Where a single-session price is published, thirty minutes costs $25 to $40 at most places, and forty-five minutes $35 to $50. The lowest published price is $25 for thirty minutes, at Zen Zone in Beldon and Rhema Wellness Studio in Cockburn Central. Prices checked October 2026 on the places' own websites.

faq.q: How long is an infrared sauna session?
faq.a: Most Perth studios sell thirty- or forty-five-minute sessions, and some offer sixty. A combined sauna-and-ice-bath session usually runs an hour.

faq.q: What do you wear in an infrared sauna?
faq.a: Most infrared cabins in Perth are booked privately, so light clothing, swimwear or a towel is usual. Bring water, and check the place's website for whether towels are supplied.

faq.q: Can two people share an infrared sauna?
faq.a: Yes, at many places. Published two-person prices for thirty minutes include $40 at Zen Zone, $44 at The Neighbourhood Sauna, $45 at Rhema Wellness Studio and $50 at Salt Float Studio.

faq.q: Is an infrared sauna the same as a traditional sauna?
faq.a: No. A traditional sauna heats the air in a wood-lined room and runs much hotter, often as a shared room. An infrared cabin runs at a lower air temperature, is usually private, and sessions tend to be longer. Our infrared vs traditional sauna comparison sets them side by side.

faq.q: Where can I do an infrared sauna and ice bath together?
faq.a: Many recovery studios sell the two as one session. Locked In Recovery in Warwick, for example, publishes sixty minutes of sauna and ice bath for $45. The ice bath and sauna page lists every place that offers both.

intro: Compare what a steam room visit costs, what it includes and who can go, at the places Oria Haven lists. Each card and the table below show the standard adult visit that includes the steam room, as the venue publishes it, with the day it was checked.

Steam rooms in Perth usually come with something larger: a leisure centre's pool and wellness entry, a bathhouse session with saunas and cold pools, a hotel spa's retreat area, or a recovery centre's timed session. A few day spas sell steam on its own. How you get in -- a casual ticket, a treatment, a membership -- differs as much as the price.

A steam room is humid heat at a lower temperature than a sauna's dry heat. It is not the same as a steam shower, or water poured on a sauna's stones; the places here have a steam room. Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: What's the difference between a steam room and a sauna?
faq.a: A steam room fills with humid, wet heat at a lower temperature; a sauna is drier and hotter, though water poured on the stones adds steam. Saunas are listed on Saunas in Perth.

faq.q: How much does a sauna session cost in Perth?
faq.a: Where it's published: from about $25 for thirty minutes and about $35 to $45 for an hour, less for early-morning sessions at some rooms. At hotel and day spas the sauna usually comes with a treatment or a day visit rather than being sold on its own. Packs and memberships lower the per-visit price at most sauna studios.

faq.q: What's the difference between a traditional and an infrared sauna?
faq.a: A traditional sauna, often Finnish-style, heats the air in a wood-lined room. An infrared sauna uses infrared panels and runs at a lower air temperature, so sessions tend to be longer. Both are listed here, and each listing says which it has.

faq.q: Are there private saunas in Perth?
faq.a: Yes. Several places book a sauna room for one or two people, or hire it out to a group, rather than sharing it. Others run communal sessions, including beachside saunas and bathhouses.

faq.q: What is aufguss?
faq.a: A sauna session led by a facilitator who pours water on the stones and works the steam and scent through the room in rounds. At least one Perth sauna house builds its sessions around it.

faq.q: Where can I do a sauna and ice bath together?
faq.a: Most dedicated sauna studios have a cold plunge or ice bath too. The places set up to alternate the two in one session are listed under Ice bath & sauna together (contrast therapy).

intro: {count} places in Perth list cryotherapy: Perth Cryo in Currambine, Element Health Centres in Claremont, Mindbody Lounge in Victoria Park and Recovery Haus in Innaloo. It is not an ice bath. Instead of sitting in cold water, you stand in a chamber of very cold, dry air for a few minutes. Element Health Centres, for example, runs whole-body sessions of up to three minutes at temperatures down to −87.5°C. Some places also offer localised cryotherapy, which cools one area rather than the whole body.

All four are recovery studios rather than cryotherapy-only clinics, so the chamber sits alongside things like an infrared sauna, compression boots, red light or hyperbaric oxygen. Most sell it in packs or memberships that cover several of them.

Where prices are published, Mindbody Lounge sells session credits that work out at $33 to $40 a session depending on the pack, and Perth Cryo's packages start from $60. Element Health Centres sells weekly memberships and multi-week programmes rather than single sessions. Prices change, so check with the place before you book.
Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: Is cryotherapy the same as an ice bath?
faq.a: No. Cryotherapy is a few minutes in a chamber of very cold, dry air; an ice bath or cold plunge is cold water you sit in. If you're after cold water, see ice baths and cold plunges in Perth.

faq.q: How long is a cryotherapy session?
faq.a: Short. Element Health Centres publishes sessions of up to three minutes. Most places don't publish a length, so ask when you book.

faq.q: How much does cryotherapy cost in Perth?
faq.a: Where it's published, Mindbody Lounge's session credits work out at $33 to $40 a session, and Perth Cryo's packages start from $60. Some places only sell memberships or programmes. Check the place's own site for current prices.

faq.q: Where can I try cryotherapy in Perth?
faq.a: Perth Cryo in Currambine, Element Health Centres in Claremont, Mindbody Lounge in Victoria Park and Recovery Haus in Innaloo all list it. Each listing links to the place's own booking page.

intro: {count} places in Perth list red light therapy. Almost all are recovery studios, float centres or wellness spas that offer it beside a sauna, ice bath or compression boots. It is a light session, not a cold one, so if you came looking for cold therapy, ice baths and cold plunges have their own page.

The equipment varies. Several places use a full-body bed you lie in, such as the TheraLight 360 at Mindbody Lounge in Victoria Park and the full-body bed at Reclab in Wembley. Element Health Centres publishes 20-minute full-body sessions. Others use smaller targeted devices, like the handheld units at My Recovery Club in Harrisdale, and Beyond Rest in East Perth offers red light as a body-contouring service.

Single-session prices are rarely published. Red light is usually sold in packs or memberships that cover several pieces of equipment; Mindbody Lounge's session credits, for example, work out at $33 to $40 a session. Check the place's own site for current prices.
Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, or you're pregnant or unsure, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner before you book.

faq.q: Is red light therapy the same as an infrared sauna?
faq.a: No, it's different equipment. An infrared sauna is a heated cabin you sit in; red light therapy uses a bed, panel or handheld device fitted with LEDs. Many Perth recovery studios offer both.

faq.q: How long is a red light session?
faq.a: Element Health Centres publishes 20 minutes for a full-body session. Most places don't publish a length, so ask when you book.

faq.q: How much does red light therapy cost in Perth?
faq.a: Few places publish a single-session price; most sell red light within packs or memberships. Mindbody Lounge's session credits work out at $33 to $40 a session. Check the place's own site for current prices.
